newsitem.title: USA: CRP has 3.4 mln fewer acres in wheat states - NAWG.
newsitem.headline: CRP has 3.4 mln fewer acres in wheat states - NAWG.

text.p: The latest Conservation Reserve Program (CRP) signup shows 3.4 million fewer acres will be included in the government's long-term land idling program in major wheat states but more acres may be idled this year, the National Association of Wheat Growers (NAWG) said.
"Wheat producers who did not make the cut can now either prepare to plant or prepare a new offer for the next signup," NAWG president Phil McLain said in a statement.

Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman last Thursday said 16.1 million acres would be accepted into the CRP this fall, when 21.1 million acres expire. A total of 11.7 million acres were re-enrolled, 9.5 million acres returned to production, and 4.4 million new acres accepted.
Farmers offered 25.6 million acres to be idled during a signup in March. The CRP pays farmers an annual rent to take fragile lands out of production for 10 years.
Among wheat states, CRP acres rose in both North and South Dakota but Texas saw a drop of more than one million CRP acres, Minnesota 770,000 and Washington 613,000, NAWG said.
"The Secretary has accepted 16 million acres into the program, but there's room for more," NAWG vice president Carl Schwensen said.

The NAWG praised Glickman for announcing the signup by the end of May and for adding another opportunity for farmers to sign up acres in CRP this fall. But it said Glickman should not wait until the fall to sign up more acres.
"The 16th signup should be available for land under CRP contracts that will expire October 1, 1998, as well as land not accepted in the 15th signup," Schwensen said.

Schwensen said winter wheat producers would have to decide on planting and field preparations ahead of autumn, so waiting until fall for the next signup would handicap them in deciding whether to include more wheat acreage in the next CRP.
